column1: # Giauque W.F., Egan C.J. (1937). Carbon Dioxide. The Heat Capacity and Vapor Pressure of the Solid. The Heat of
# Sublimation. Thermodynamic and Spectroscopic Values of the Entropy. J. Chem. Phys. 5, 45-54. doi:10.1063/1.1749929.
# AIP copyright, owner-provided. Pages 50 to 52 (PDF pages 7 to 9). Tables I and VII read from 200-220 dpi renders,
# Tables IV and V from the text layer, with Table V checked against a 130 dpi render.
# Temperature scale: 0 C = 273.10 K (as printed; ICT-era scale, not ITS-90).
# block VP  = Table I, "Vapor pressure of solid carbon dioxide", p. 50: T in K; P observed in international cm Hg
#             (standard gravity 980.665 cm/s2); dP = P obs - P calc and dT = T obs - T calc against their eq. (1),
#             Normal sublimation point from eq. (1): 194.67 +- 0.05 K. The paper: "the absolute temperatures may be in
#             error by several hundredths of a degree"; T given to 0.001 K for relative accuracy. 12 points.
#             P_kPa is derived here (cm Hg x 1.333224), not printed.
# block CP_OBS = Table IV, "Heat capacity of solid carbon dioxide (molecular weight, 44.00)", p. 51: T in K, approximate
#             temperature rise dT_K of each measurement, Cp in cal(15 C)/(deg mol); 1 cal = 4.185 abs J (p. 52).
#             41 points, 15.52 to 189.78 K. Stated accuracy +-0.2 % from 35 to 195 K, +-1 % at 20 K, +-3 % at 15 K.
# block CP_SMOOTH = Table V, "values taken from a smooth curve through observations", p. 52: Cp in cal/(deg mol) at round
#             T, 15 to 190 K (22 values); dev_EEH_pct = Eucken, Eucken and Hauck minus this research, %;
#             dev_MB_pct = Maass and Barnes minus this research, %.
# block DHSUB = Table VII, "Heat of sublimation of carbon dioxide", p. 52: calorimetric enthalpy of sublimation at 760 mm Hg
#             and the sublimation temperature 194.67 K, cal/mol; moles sublimed and time of energy input in the extra
#             columns. Mean 6030 +- 5 cal/mol = 25 236 +- 21 J/mol with 4.185 J/cal (conversion derived here). Superheating
#             corrections of 0.2 to 1.6 cal/mol (Table VI) are applied. Their 6029 cal/mol from eq. (1) plus Berthelot is
#             given "no weight" against the calorimetric value.
# Sanity check: eq. (1) at 194.67 K gives 75.99 cm Hg (1 atm = 76.00 cm); Cp rises monotonically with T in both Cp blocks.
# Digits as printed, one sanity check, not re-verified (owner: not looking for 100 % correct data).
# Role: G4 pure-CO2 holdout (sublimation pressure, sublimation enthalpy target, crystal Cp). Transcribed 2026-09-25,
